messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: spikes in 5xx and error-rate on /v1/generate -> router initiated fallback to regional variants (policy:region_fallback_v2). autoscaler reports pool 'dedicated-west-3' draining. incident id: INC-20240210-77

maria (oncall): seeing it. UI shows ~30% 503 on requests routed to dedicated-west-3, latency up across same pool. Is this the oxford change from last night?

aj: not that change. I rolled back variant pinning in canary. Looks like router telemetry is flipping between capacity signals for the dedicated pool.

jason: paging @li for metrics/infra help — looks like the router consumed a noisy metric (kernel io wait spike) and thought nodes were unhealthy, so it started sending traffic to fallback variants. When fallback destinations filled up, errors climbed.

li: on it. pulling p99/5xx dashboards. `sum(rate(router.5xx[5m])) by (pool,region)` shows a hard jump starting 18:02 UTC. But `node_exporter:cpu_iowait` is spiking on only 2/12 GPUs in the pool.

maria (oncall): customer-impact? CS bot, any reports?

customer-success-bot: Automated CS digest: 8 customer-facing requests flagged low-responses (chat completions) from multiple tenants on us-west. No active escalations yet.

aj: hypothesis: a noisy node caused autoscaler to mis-evaluate aggregate pool capacity because our weight calc uses median latency + node health flags. The router then rolled variants to region fallback policy which cascaded.

sre-bot: NOTE: fallback policy 'region_fallback_v2' has a roll_limit of 2 and will automatically reassign if eligible pools drop below threshold. This can cause oscillation if signal flips quickly.

maria (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) stop further automatic rollouts -> disable fallback policy on router. 2) mark problematic nodes as unsched to drain gracefully. 3) scale up reserved capacity in unaffected pool to absorb traffic. 4) follow up with dev infra for metric calibration.

aj: agree. disabling fallback now on router control plane: `curl -X POST "https://router-control/api/policies/region_fallback_v2/disable" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`

oncall-bot: ACTION: policy region_fallback_v2 disabled by aj at 18:12 UTC. Router will stop initiating further fallbacks.

li: marking GPUs g2 and g5 in dedicated-west-3 as maintenance: `infractl node annotate gpu-wn-12 "maintenance=io_spike"` then `k8s cordon gpu-wn-12 && k8s drain gpu-wn-12 --ignore-daemonsets`

jason: scaling dedicated-west-1 pool by +3 machines via infra autoserve: `infra-cli scale pool dedicated-west-1 --add 3` to give headroom for steady traffic while drains finish.

maria (oncall): routing metrics now look better — 5xx rate dropping back to baseline after disabling policy and scaling. Still seeing a backlog of queued requests in router (queue depth ~1200) for 10 minutes.

aj: to clear queues safely, enabling small burst capacity on dedicated-west-1: `routerctl set-burst dedicated-west-1 200` and reduce batching window from 50ms to 20ms for next 10min.

li: logs from the problematic nodes show repeated kernel block device timeouts and heavy host NVMe GC cycles: http://logs.redwood/host/gpu-wn-12/2024-02-10. Suspect a host-level firmware/driver issue.

customer-success-bot: Sent a proactive message to affected customers: "We're investigating increased error rates for completions in US-West. We're routing to alternative capacity and will update in 30min."

maria (oncall): handoff note incoming in 20. @aj will continue mitigation, I'll take shift handover with pagerduty.

pagerduty: PAGED @maria (oncall) for incident INC-20240210-77 at 18:28 UTC (high).

maria (oncall): summary for next oncall: we disabled the region fallback policy to stop oscillation, cordoned 2 noisy GPUs in dedicated-west-3, scaled dedicated-west-1 +3, and set burst capacity to drain router queues. Customer impact: elevated 5xx and latency for ~25min, now degrading toward baseline. Next steps: monitor p95/p99 on /v1/generate, coordinate with infra to investigate host-level NVMe/firmware on the drained nodes, and consider lowering sensitivity on router health scoring to avoid median-based flips.

aj: filing follow-up bug for policy mode: policy should have a cooldown window and require stable node-level signals for >=1m before roll. Also add hysteresis to autoscaler signals. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/router/pulls/2457

li: infra ticket created: INFRA-5231 "Investigate NVMe GC causing iowait spikes on dedicated-west-3 hosts". Marked as sev3; assigned to storage team.

jason: will roll a temporary firmware downgrade on the two affected hosts in maintenance once drains complete, planned at 19:00 UTC if storage team approves.

maria (oncall): last checks at 18:53 UTC -> router 5xx at baseline, queue depth down to 130, p95 latency back to +10% above normal. Leaving incident open for postmortem. Handing to @aj for follow-up.

aj: ack. I'll keep watch for 2h then close. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-20240210-77 status -> mitigated (policy disable + pool ops). Next update scheduled 2h.

customer-success-bot: Updated customers: "Issue mitigated, we routed traffic and are investigating root cause. We'll share postmortem and timeline"

maria (oncall): end handoff. I'm putting final notes in the incident tracker and capturing the exact timeline.

jason: quick note for postmortem: include timeline of autoscaler signal, router decision logs, and the queue pressure timeline. Also include cost impact from burst scaling.

li: saving key logs to s3: `aws s3 cp /var/logs/gpu-wn-12 s3://redwood-incidents/INC-20240210-77/gpu-wn-12/ --recursive`

oncall-bot: Thread closed for live mitigation. Postmortem required.
